hypothesis: ProductStart V4 can report PASS for an otherwise identical snapshot that adds a service RootDirectory because V2/V3/V4 do not observe or constrain that namespace semantic.
strongest_counterhypothesis: The existing unit fragment hash and argv binding may already be sufficient because a namespace-changing setting would necessarily alter the hashed unit fragment and therefore be represented by the ProductStart identity anchor.
counterhypothesis_analysis: A fragment hash binds the configured unit bytes only after the owner chooses and provisions that identity. V4 does not impose a semantic invariant that alternate service roots/path substitutions are forbidden, so an owner-pinned but semantically unsafe unit could still satisfy the hash relation. The repair therefore constrains semantics in addition to bytes.
